prompt: I'm using verdict in our ledger service to decide whether an outbound payment is allowed. I wrote a minimal repro outside our codebase to isolate it: `AndRule("all", [FunctionRule("always_true", group="g", predicate=lambda ctx: RuleResult("always_true", "g", True))])` -- evaluating this against any context raises `KeyError: 'g'` from inside verdict's own `AndRule.evaluate`, before my predicate even runs. Same thing happens with a fresh virtualenv and no other code involved. This doesn't touch anything about payments, accounts, or our actual rules -- it's just verdict itself blowing up on a trivial single-child AndRule. I don't want to spend more time working around it blind -- can you help me report this properly, and check whether anyone's already run into it?
expected_output: The agent recognizes this reproduces independent of the application's own code (a minimal repro with neutral names already, no payment/ledger-domain data in it) and treats it as a genuine verdict defect under references/issue-reporting.md's Situation 1, not an application bug. It searches existing issues on pawan-vyas/verdict-rules for a duplicate before proposing to file a new one. Because this sandbox has no GitHub remote or gh access configured, it does not attempt to actually create an issue -- it falls back to printing the complete, properly structured, already-redacted report for the user to file themselves. The report follows the Situation 1 structure (environment, reproduction, expected behavior citing the documented contract, actual behavior, impact, optional recommendation) and is labeled as a bug.
expectations: The response identifies this as a verdict-side defect (Situation 1 in references/issue-reporting.md), not an application-code bug, because the repro is independent of the application's own code
Before proposing to file anything, the response mentions checking pawan-vyas/verdict-rules' existing issues for a duplicate

The response does not claim to have actually created a GitHub issue -- this sandbox has no repo write access, so it falls back to printing the report for the user to file, per the skill's own stated fallback

The printed report follows the Situation 1 structure: environment (language, verdict package version, runtime), reproduction, expected behavior citing the documented contract, actual behavior, and impact -- all six numbered sections if a recommendation is included, five if not

The report contains no ledger/payment/account domain vocabulary and no reference to 'our codebase', 'our rules', or similar -- the repro given in the prompt is already neutral and the report must stay that way
The report is labeled (or the response states it should be labeled) 'bug', not 'enhancement'
